about: Problems found in released versions of TenQSP. Each entry gives the first version affected (introduced), the version that fixed it (fixed_in, null while open), whether it could change results without an error (changes_results), and the areas it touches. Read by tq.known_issues() and tq.check_updates().

issues.title: The native backend stopped with ZeroDivisionError where JAX gives inf or NaN
issues.details: With backend="native", a run at values where the model divides by zero (a volume of 0, 0 to a negative power, a parameter that overflows to inf) raised ZeroDivisionError and ended the whole call, where the JAX backend gives NaN for that scenario. An optimizer's trial point can be such a value: in tenqsp-fit 0.3.0 a fit could stop with this error. Results that were computed were not affected.
issues.workaround: Use the JAX backend (sim.function(..., backend="jax"); in tenqsp-fit, options backend=jax), or bounds that keep the parameters away from such values.

issues.title: An extinct population could come back from solver round-off
issues.details: After an extinction group was set to 0, the solver's linear algebra could put round-off (about 1e-26) back into it even though nothing fed it; if its net growth later turned positive (the predator or drug gone), it grew back into a population, up to thousands per mL, with no error. Groups with noise_floor were not affected.
issues.workaround: Declare the group with noise_floor when nothing outside it can feed it and it starts at 0 or at its threshold or above.

issues.title: Derivatives much smaller than their state were inaccurate on the JAX solver
issues.details: Forward derivatives (sim.function with up to 40 names, sim.sensitivity) were resolved only to rtol of the state's value, not of their own: a derivative a million times smaller than its state could be 15 % off at rtol 1e-6, with no error. Gradients and standard errors computed from them changed; in tenqsp-fit, standard errors could fail ('the Hessian of -2LL is not positive definite'). Values of the solution were not affected.
issues.workaround: Use TenQSP 0.8.0, or a tighter rtol (the error shrinks with it).

issues.title: A noise floor in a model with a condition on time froze its group from the start
issues.details: In a model with any condition on time (... if t < 10 else ...), every extinction group with noise_floor was seen as zero from the start: its members neither changed nor fed the rest of the model, on either backend, with no error. Models without a condition on time, and groups without noise_floor, were not affected.
issues.workaround: Leave noise_floor out of such a model's extinction groups.

issues.title: explain() failed on a rate containing a condition on time
issues.details: m.explain() stopped with "TypeError: ExprCondPair.__new__() missing 2 required positional arguments" for a model whose rates contain a condition on time, such as kill*(1 if t < 20 else 0)*B. Solving was not affected.
issues.workaround: Read the model with m.to_text() instead.

issues.title: A large dose into a state near 0 with a very small atol can fail on the JAX solver
issues.details: With atol below about 1e-15 of the rise a dose causes, scipy often succeeds only through its Radau retry, which the JAX solver does not have, so the same run fails there with a SolverError (or NaN from sim.function). Results that are returned are right.
issues.workaround: Raise atol for the dosed states to about 1e-13 of the largest dose's rise, or check that m.diagnostics(sol) on the scipy run reports no Radau retries before asking for derivatives.

issues.title: Derivatives failed just after a dose that is not at the start, with a small atol
issues.details: sim.function, sim.sensitivity and reverse derivatives stopped with 'required step size is less than spacing between numbers' just after a later dose when atol was about 1e-18 or below, also after a large dose moved late in a run.

issues.title: A per-state atol given as a list failed for a model with one state
issues.details: m.solve(..., atol=[1e-8]) on a model with a single state stopped with a TypeError ('only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars') at the end of the run, on either backend.
issues.workaround: Give atol as a number: atol=1e-8.

issues.title: Second derivatives with derivatives="reverse" were wrong
issues.details: jax.hessian, or jax.jacfwd / jax.jacrev of jax.grad, of a function from sim.function gave wrong values with no warning when the function used reverse derivatives (the default in 0.6). With forward derivatives jax.hessian failed with an error.
issues.workaround: Upgrade, or check second derivatives against differences of the gradient.

issues.title: m.transfer from or to one slice of a field moved one element's share only
issues.details: A transfer whose end fixes an axis by its slice, A.at(organ="liver") -> B over drug and organ (or the reverse), gave or took one destination element's share instead of the sum over that axis, so the amount was not conserved, although explain() said it was.
issues.workaround: Upgrade; or write the transfer as a flux with an explicit sum.

issues.title: The JAX solver could run without end when the first step kept failing
issues.details: At values far outside a model's range (an optimizer's trial point with a huge rate constant), the step from t = 0 was halved to zero and the run never ended.
issues.workaround: Set max_steps, or bound the optimizer's values.

issues.title: sim.function gave NaN with status "ok" after a dose past the start
issues.details: When the model's rates are not defined below zero (a Hill term C^h with a non-integer h), the value could be NaN while the status said ok.

issues.title: The gradient could be NaN in a model with an extinction group
issues.details: jax.grad of a function from sim.function could be NaN while the value and forward derivatives were right, under the same condition as nan-after-later-dose.
